root_cause.text: The RISC-V IOMMU paging-domain code updated DDT/PDT entries in riscv_iommu_iodir_update() without issuing the specification-required IOTINVAL invalidations, leaving stale IOMMU TLB/context-cache state referencing old directory entries.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly says to “perform required TLB and context cache invalidations after updating DDT or PDT entries,” and the patch adds a new riscv_iommu_iodir_iotinval() helper and calls it immediately after each DDT invalidation command in riscv_iommu_iodir_update().

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The RISC-V IOMMU paging-domain code updated DDT/PDT entries in riscv_iommu_iodir_update() without issuing the specification-required IOTINVAL invalidations, leaving stale IOMMU TLB/context-cache state referencing old directory entries.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit explicitly says to “perform required TLB and context cache invalidations after updating DDT or PDT entries,” and the patch adds a new riscv_iommu_iodir_iotinval() helper and calls it immediately after each DDT invalidation command in riscv_iommu_iodir_update().

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a helper to issue spec-compliant RISC-V IOMMU IOTINVAL commands after DDT/PDT updates so stale translation state is properly invalidated.
intent_record.what: A new static helper function, riscv_iommu_iodir_iotinval(), was added along with a descriptive comment. The function builds an IOTINVAL.VMA command, conditionally sets PSCID and/or GSCID fields based on whether iohgatp is in BARE mode, whether a PDT invalidation is requested, and fields in the provided dc and pc structures, then sends the command with riscv_iommu_cmd_send().
intent_record.how: This adds the runtime logic needed to issue the RISC-V IOMMU invalidation command sequence required after DDT or PDT entry updates, choosing the proper invalidation scope for bare versus non-bare IOHGATP modes and for PDT versus non-PDT cases. It ensures address-translation-related cached state is invalidated correctly after directory changes, preventing stale IOMMU translations or context from being used.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an IO translation invalidation after DDT invalidation in riscv_iommu_iodir_update to properly flush device translation state with the current default non-SVA/PASID setup.
intent_record.what: A call to riscv_iommu_iodir_iotinval(iommu, false, dc->iohgatp, dc, NULL) was added inside the loop in riscv_iommu_iodir_update() immediately after sending the DDT invalidation command, along with a comment explaining that SVA and PASID are not yet merged so inval_pdt is false and pc is NULL.
intent_record.how: At runtime, each IODIR update now triggers an additional IO translation invalidation using the device context's iohgatp after the DDT invalidation command is sent, ensuring related cached translation state is also invalidated under the current non-SVA, non-PASID configuration.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an IOTINVAL invalidation after each DDT invalidation during IODIR updates to properly flush IOMMU translation state for current non-SVA/non-PASID setups.
intent_record.what: A call to riscv_iommu_iodir_iotinval(iommu, false, dc->iohgatp, dc, NULL) was added inside the existing loop in riscv_iommu_iodir_update() immediately after sending the IODIR invalidate DDT command, along with a comment stating that SVA and PASID are not yet merged so inval_pdt is false and pc is NULL.
intent_record.how: At runtime, each device context update now triggers an additional IOTINVAL invalidation using the current iohgatp and device context after the DDT invalidation command is sent, ensuring related IOMMU translation state is also invalidated under the current non-SVA/non-PASID configuration instead of only issuing the DDT invalidate command.

grouping_result.intent: Add an IOTINVAL invalidation after each DDT invalidation during IODIR updates to properly flush IOMMU translation state for current non-SVA/non-PASID setups.

consistency_review.core_intent: Add spec-compliant IOTINVAL invalidation alongside existing DDT/PDT invalidations during RISC-V IOMMU IODIR-related updates so stale IO translation state is flushed in the current non-SVA/non-PASID configuration.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly add the missing spec-required IOTINVAL invalidations after DDT/PDT updates in riscv_iommu_iodir_update(), which matches the root cause of stale IOMMU translation/cache state caused by updating directory entries without those invalidations.

candidates.rationale: This sends only the DDT invalidation command during IODIR update. Per the root cause, updating DDT/PDT entries without the required IOTINVAL left stale translation/context state active.
This is the pre-fix send of the directory invalidation command in the other update path, again lacking the required follow-up IOTINVAL invalidation, which is the direct cause of stale IOMMU state.

The code invalidates only the DDT entry after an IODIR update. The root cause is that this invalidation alone is insufficient without the spec-required IOTINVAL to flush stale translation/context cache state.
This line shows the pre-fix logic performing only DDT invalidation during IODIR updates. The missing IOTINVAL after this operation is what allowed stale entries to persist.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement issues only a DDT invalidation after updating directory entries. Per the root cause, DDT/PDT updates also required a specification-mandated IOTINVAL to flush stale translation/context-cache state; performing only this invalidation left old mappings active.

This sends the incomplete invalidation sequence consisting only of the DDT invalidation command. Because no follow-up IOTINVAL was issued, stale IOMMU TLB/context-cache state could continue referencing old directory entries after the update.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body for `riscv_iommu_iodir_update()` is sufficient because it contains the DDT/device-context update sequence and the associated invalidation handling. The root cause says the vulnerability exists when DDT/PDT entries are updated 'without issuing the specification-required IOTINVAL invalidations'. In this snippet, invalidation is explicitly present both before and after updating device context entries. First, for each valid existing context, the code clears `DC_TC_V` with `WRITE_ONCE(dc->tc, tc & ~RISCV_IOMMU_DC_TC_V);` and immediately issues directory invalidation commands: `riscv_iommu_cmd_iodir_inval_ddt(&cmd);`, `riscv_iommu_cmd_iodir_set_did(&cmd, fwspec->ids[i]);`, `riscv_iommu_cmd_send(iommu, &cmd);`, followed by `if (sync_required) riscv_iommu_cmd_sync(iommu, RISCV_IOMMU_IOTINVAL_TIMEOUT);`. Then after rewriting the context (`WRITE_ONCE(dc->tc, tc);`) it again performs `riscv_iommu_cmd_iodir_inval_ddt(&cmd);`, `riscv_iommu_cmd_iodir_set_did(&cmd, fwspec->ids[i]);`, `riscv_iommu_cmd_send(iommu, &cmd);` and finally `riscv_iommu_cmd_sync(iommu, RISCV_IOMMU_IOTINVAL_TIMEOUT);`. Therefore the vulnerable construct 'update directory entries without required invalidation' is absent here, and the function already contains the fix logic of issuing invalidation and synchronization around the update.
